title: Is making a custom menu via plugin doable / worth it ?

posts.author: static_remains
posts.body:
I’ve gathered some plugins to make the default menu look better (some are from visustella) but have become kind of frustrated that I can’t do much besides change the background and colors of the menu at the moment.
I drafted how I want my new menu to look and know that there are ways to make custom menu visuals through eventing, but I’m worried that I will somehow leave some terrible gap in the code that causes a game breaking bug over something as simple as a menu…
Are there plugins to make custom menus or is that the type of thing you commission?  Or is it something not worth the time spent because it will strain MZ’s resources … Sorry for the rambling, I’m just not sure if I should keep pursuing this idea since I don’t know where to go.
If you read this far, thank you

posts.author: Kenen
posts.body:
Custom UI work tends to be very code-heavy while simultaneously being very subjective for the end-user, which is in part why you don't see a lot of public plugins that offer deep UI customization.
A custom UI is a prime candidate for something to commission for the reasons above, but before you think about it, I'd suggest making sure you have a fully fleshed-out mockup (or series of mockups) created in Photoshop/Gimp/etc. to increase your chances of a successful commission.
One thing to note is that if you are deeply invested in the VisuStella ecosystem, you will need to consider their code obfuscation practices and whether or not their window extensions/additions can be easily styled by another developer. You might not want your custom UI to look awkward if you have a window added by VisuStella plugins that your commissioned developer isn't able to readily modify or style.

posts.author: Winshifter
posts.body:
Visustella gives you a lot of customization to the UI, but at the same time it has its limitations, because you only have the options they have allowed you to modify. Though with some very good modifications, even with what they allow you to do, you can almost make it way different than what they show in their videos or what you might think, though you might need additional plugins other than the Menu one.
If you require a serious change on how the UI looks or its functions, you might need to have someone code it basically from scratch or event it the way you want it.
Regarding eventing a Menu. Unless you do something too weird, normally you shouldn't have any kind of weird bug that might break the game. In the hype of the Rpg Maker 2003 era, there were a lot of games with Custom Menu Systems and they rarely had any bug that would break your game, at worst would give you things you shouldn't have yet or didn't have a particular image file that kind of blocked you...though most of the time it was on how code on Rm2k3 was kind of weird sometimes.
